subject: chemistry
title: Empirical and molecular formulae
key_idea: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound. A molecular formula gives the actual number of atoms in one molecule. It is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula.

blocks.text: The same compound can be written in two ways. One shows the simplest ratio of atoms. The other shows the real numbers in a molecule.

items.meaning: The simplest whole number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule.

blocks.text: From a molecular formula to an empirical formula

items: Find the number that divides exactly into every number of atoms.
Divide each number by it.
Butane, C₄H₁₀: divide both numbers by 2 to get C₂H₅.

blocks.text: From an empirical formula to a molecular formula

blocks.label: Number of empirical units in a molecule
blocks.formula: n = Mr of the molecule ÷ Mr of the empirical formula
where: n is a whole number with no unit.
Multiply every number in the empirical formula by n.

items: Empirical formula CH₂ has Mr = 12 + 2 = 14.
A hydrocarbon with Mr = 56 has n = 56 ÷ 14 = 4, so its molecular formula is C₄H₈.

diagram.alt: Find the number of carbon atoms in a molecule from its relative formula mass.
diagram.question: A hydrocarbon has the empirical formula CH₂ and a relative formula mass of {mr}. How many carbon atoms are in one molecule? (Relative atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1)
working: The molecular formula is C{answer}H(2 × {answer}), so it has {answer} carbon atoms.

items: Empirical formula: simplest whole number ratio. Molecular formula: actual numbers of atoms.
To go from empirical to molecular, divide the molecule's Mr by the empirical Mr and multiply.

sections.heading: Finding an empirical formula from masses

blocks.text: An empirical formula can be worked out from the masses of the elements in a sample, or from percentages.

items.text: For percentages, treat them as masses in 100 g.
Divide each mass by the relative atomic mass of the element.
Divide the results by the smallest one to get the simplest whole number ratio.
Use the ratio as the numbers in the formula.

blocks.label: Worked example: 1.20 g of magnesium and 3.55 g of chlorine
where: Ar of Mg = 24.0 and Ar of Cl = 35.5.

items: Divide by Ar, not the other way round. Dividing Ar by mass gives the wrong ratio.
Show the working. A formula with no working scores no marks.
If the ratio is not whole, such as 1 : 1.5, multiply to get whole numbers. 1 : 1.5 becomes 2 : 3.

diagram.alt: Divide a mass by its relative atomic mass.
diagram.question: A compound contains {m} g of an element with relative atomic mass {ar}. Calculate mass ÷ Ar for this element. Give the answer to 3 decimal places.
working: Divide the mass of the element by its Ar.

items: Divide each mass by Ar, then divide by the smallest to find the ratio.
The ratio must be whole numbers. Multiply up if it is not.
Show the working. The formula alone scores no marks.

blocks.text: Heating magnesium in a crucible shows that magnesium and oxygen combine in a fixed ratio. The results give the empirical formula of magnesium oxide.

items.text: Find the mass of a crucible and lid.
Put a known mass of magnesium in the crucible, put the lid on and weigh again.
Heat strongly for several minutes. Let in a little air by lifting the lid slightly.
Let the crucible, lid and contents cool, then find the mass.
Reheat and weigh again. Repeat until the mass stops changing.

items: The increase in mass is the mass of oxygen that combined with the magnesium.
Heating until the mass stays constant shows that all the magnesium has reacted.
Divide the mass of magnesium by 24 and the mass of oxygen by 16 to find the ratio. It is 1 : 1, so the formula is MgO.
Smoke leaving the crucible makes the mass of oxide too low.
The mass gained is oxygen. Heat to constant mass to be sure the reaction is complete.
Divide each mass by its Ar to find the ratio of atoms.

checks.q: Give the empirical formula of butene, C₄H₈.
0.92 g of sodium combines with 0.32 g of oxygen. Calculate the empirical formula of the oxide. (Ar: Na = 23, O = 16)
checks.a: 0.92 ÷ 23 = 0.04 and 0.32 ÷ 16 = 0.02. The ratio is 2 : 1, so the formula is Na₂O.

checks.q: A compound has the empirical formula CH₂O and a relative formula mass of 180. Calculate its molecular formula. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
checks.a: Mr of CH₂O = 30. 180 ÷ 30 = 6. The molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.

exam_phrases: (which) act in all directions (in the giant structure)
large amounts of energy needed to break the bonds / forces

mistakes.wrong: Aluminium oxide has a high melting point because of its strong ionic bonds.
mistakes.right: Strong ionic bonds is ignored. Say there are strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions.

mistakes.wrong: Sodium chloride is held together by molecules.
mistakes.right: Sodium chloride is a giant structure of ions held by electrostatic attractions. It does not contain molecules.

mistakes.wrong: Ionic compounds melt easily because the lattice is only held by weak forces.
mistakes.right: The forces are strong and act in all directions, so large amounts of energy are needed to break them.

worked_example.question: Explain why copper oxide (CuO) has a high melting point.
answer_points: There are strong (electrostatic) forces of attraction (1)
so large amounts of energy are needed to break the many strong bonds or forces (1)
worked_example.tip: Allow: large amounts of energy are needed to break the forces in all directions, or the bonds in the lattice.

blocks.text: An ionic compound is a giant structure of ions. Strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions hold it together. These forces act in all directions in the lattice.

items: You can work out the empirical formula of an ionic compound from a model or diagram that shows its ions.
Count the ions of each type, then write the simplest whole number ratio. Sodium chloride has equal numbers of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, so its formula is NaCl.
A diagram shows only part of a giant structure. This is one limit of dot and cross, ball and stick, and 2D or 3D diagrams.

exam_phrases: until mass remains constant / heat to constant mass
full marks can only be obtained with working shown

mistakes.wrong: MgCl₂ (the formula alone, with no working).
mistakes.right: The formula without working scores 0. Show the division by Ar, the ratio and then the formula.
Fractions are inverted. Divide the mass by the Ar, such as 1.20 ÷ 24.0. The inverted fractions do not score the ratio mark.

mistakes.wrong: Continue heating the magnesium until it no longer glows or it all turns white.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Reheat, record the mass, and repeat until the mass remains constant.

worked_example.question:
1.20 g of magnesium reacts completely with 3.55 g of chlorine to form magnesium chloride.

Calculate the empirical formula of the magnesium chloride.

(relative atomic masses: Mg = 24.0, Cl = 35.5)

You must show your working.
answer_points: Divide by atomic mass: Mg 1.20 ÷ 24.0 and Cl 3.55 ÷ 35.5 (1)
worked_example.tip: MgCl₂ without working scores 0. Follow-through marks are allowed from the first step.

exam_phrases: empirical formula of decene (C₁₀H₂₀) is CH₂
empirical formula of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) is HO
empirical formula of butane (C₄H₁₀) is C₂H₅
molecular formula from empirical formula CH₂O and Mr 180
simplest whole number ratio of atoms

mistakes.wrong: The empirical formula of butane is C₄H₁₀.
mistakes.right: That is the molecular formula. Divide both numbers by 2 to get the empirical formula C₂H₅.

mistakes.wrong: The empirical formula of hydrogen peroxide is H₂O₂.
mistakes.right: H₂O₂ is the molecular formula. The simplest ratio is 1 : 1, so the empirical formula is HO.

mistakes.wrong: The molecular formula of a compound with empirical formula CH₂ and Mr 126 is CH₂.
mistakes.right: Mr of CH₂ is 14. Divide 126 by 14 to get 9, so the molecular formula is C₉H₁₈.

worked_example.question:
The empirical formula of a compound is CH₂O.

The relative formula mass of the compound is 180.0.

What is the molecular formula of the compound?

Relative atomic mass (Ar): C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0
worked_example.tip: This is a multiple-choice question in the paper. The method is the same without the options.
